correctness.rationale: For d>1, the logarithmic derivative (d-1)/x-p x^(p-1)/a^p has the unique zero m=a((d-1)/p)^(1/p) and changes sign there. The normalized density at r=(x/m)^p is exp((d-1)/p*(log r-r+1)); setting it to y gives r exp(-r)=e^-1 y^(p/(d-1)). Both branches W0 and W-1 exist exactly for y in (0,1), and x_±=m[-W_{0,-1}(z)]^(1/p) lie on the proper sides of m. Their difference and the ratio yield stated width and octave bandwidth, including p=1 gamma limit. Independently checked 3 nongamma (d,p,a,y) cases with direct density ratios (0.4,0.5,0.73) to near machine precision. All arguments are analytic, not inferred from samples.
